title: Mini Orbit Stabilizer: cohort fingerprint leases + deterministic rollback playbook
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: We continue to see intermittent failures during multi-stage canaries where transient cohort imbalance (short-lived traffic bursts tied to session affinity) causes noisy metrics and premature rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight "cohort fingerprint" lease plus a deterministic rollback playbook that stabilizes small staged rollouts without locking long-lived resources. Motivation: reduce false-positive rollbacks, keep canaries short-lived and low-cost, and provide an auditable deterministic decision path for SREs to replay. What changed (high-level): 1) add cohort fingerprinting service: ephemeral, namespaced leases that bind a cohort fingerprint to a rollout epoch for 60s by default; 2) rollout controller uses leases to ensure metric evaluation windows compare like-for-like cohorts; 3) deterministic rollback playbook in docs that codifies when automated rollback triggers vs. when to escalate to manual abort; 4) telemetry hooks and smoke simulator to validate behavior in CI. Implementation notes: cohort fingerprint is derived from a hashed tuple (tenant_id, route_hash, epoch_id) and stored in an in-memory lease table with optional redis fallback for Private deployments. The rollout controller will reject cross-epoch comparisons if the lease mismatch rate exceeds threshold (configurable by policy). The playbook implements three rollback tiers: (A) immediate automated backout for catastrophic SLO violations, (B) auto-attenuate traffic and re-evaluate for transient spikes, (C) open an escalation with attached snapshot for human review. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing rollout semantics when the feature flag is off. Feature gating: rollout.coordinator.experimental.cohort_leases (off in production for 48 hours post-merge). Testing: unit tests for lease lifecycle, integration tests with simulated traffic bursts, and a new smoke harness that runs in CI simulating 1k requests across three cohorts to validate no-regressions. Docs: rollout/README updated with explanation and runbook at docs/runbooks/rollback-playbook.md. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (Linear ENG-4123) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards added - [x] Runbook written and reviewed - [x] Feature-flag gating in place - [x] Backward compatible defaults Release impact: Small runtime footprint, opt-in feature flag. Operators can enable per-namespace. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Canary cluster for 48h, then gradual enablement across regions. Links: design notes https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4123, smoke harness dashboard https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/rollout-smoke/mini-orbit (internal).

review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Good shape. Please add an e2e scenario where two cohorts overlap for 30s (this is our usual flaky-case).
Ava Martinez: Added overlap scenario to integration sim and added assertion for lease mismatch rate. PTAL.
Priya Kaur: Telemetry looks right. Can you make the default lease TTL configurable by env var (60s is a reasonable default but prod may want 30s)?
Ava Martinez: TTL is exposed as ROLLOUT_COHORT_LEASE_TTL with default 60. Added note in README.
Liam O'Connor: Defensive: ensure redis fallback doesn't cause false positives when network partitions occur. Suggest exponential backoff and a conservative local cache TTL.
Ava Martinez: Implemented local cache with 5s grace and exponential backoff for redis, added unit test for partition behavior.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in cohort fingerprint lease mechanism to stabilize short-lived staged rollouts and a documented deterministic rollback playbook. Feature gated and off by default. Operators can enable per-namespace. Improves false-positive rollback rate for session-affine traffic patterns.
